slides.title: Principle and source
bullets: Alkaline phosphatase hydrolyses p-nitrophenyl phosphate at pH 10.4, releasing p-nitrophenol and phosphate.
The rate of p-nitrophenol formation (405 nm) is proportional to the alkaline phosphatase activity.
ALP is high in bone, liver, placenta, intestine and kidney. Raised in Paget’s disease of bone, obstructive liver disease, hepatitis, drug hepatotoxicity and osteomalacia.

slides.title: Principle and source
bullets: This protocol follows, as an example, the instructions for use of the SPINREACT “ALP-LQ” kit (IFU BEIS44-I, 02/03/23). The IFU of your laboratory’s own kit always takes precedence: other kits may use different volumes, times, factors and reference values.

slides.title: Specimen, reagents and equipment
bullets: Specimen: unhaemolysed serum or heparinised plasma, separated from the clot quickly; stable 3 days at 2–8 °C.
R1 (buffer): diethanolamine (DEA) pH 10.4, magnesium chloride 0.5 mmol/L. R2 (substrate): p-nitrophenyl phosphate 10 mmol/L.
Equipment: spectrophotometer or analyser reading at 405 nm, 25/30/37 °C thermostat, 1.0 cm cuvettes.

slides.title: Reagent preparation (for a semi-automatic analyser)
bullets: Working reagent: 4 volumes of R1 (buffer) + 1 volume of R2 (substrate).
Working reagent stability: 1 month at 2–8 °C or 10 days at room temperature (15–25 °C).
Store the kit at 2–8 °C protected from light; particles or turbidity are signs of deterioration.

slides.title: Reagent preparation (for a semi-automatic analyser)
bullets: The values come from the SPINREACT “ALP-LQ” IFU (BEIS44-I). The IFU of the kit you use and the analyser manual always take precedence — check the programme against them.

slides.title: Procedure (manual, per the IFU)
bullets: 1. Conditions: wavelength 405 nm; constant temperature 25 °C, 30 °C or 37 °C (thermostat ± 0.1 °C).
2. Use a 1 cm cuvette; zero the instrument with distilled water or air.
3. Pipette into a cuvette: working reagent 1.2 mL + sample 20 µL.
4. Mix and wait 1 minute.

slides.title: Procedure (manual, per the IFU)
bullets: 5. Read the initial absorbance (A), start the stopwatch and read every 1 minute for 3 minutes.
6. Calculate the absorbance differences and the mean change per minute (ΔA/min).

slides.title: Semi-automatic analyser: alkaline phosphatase programme
rows: Initial A, then every 1 min for 3 min

slides.title: Calculation and result
bullets: ALP (U/L) = ΔA/min × 3300.
Temperature conversion (IFU table): result at 25 °C × 1.64 = 37 °C; at 30 °C × 1.33 = 37 °C.
Linear up to 1200 U/L; above that, dilute the sample 1/10 with NaCl 9 g/L and multiply the result by 10.

slides.title: Calculation and result
bullets: IFU reference (37 °C): adults 98–279 U/L; children (1–14 years) < 645 U/L. Exercise, periods of rapid growth in children and pregnancy affect ALP.
These values are for orientation; each laboratory should establish its own reference range.

slides.title: Interferences and errors
bullets: Fluoride, oxalate, citrate and EDTA inhibit ALP and must not be used as anticoagulants.
Haemolysis interferes because red cells contain much ALP.
Drugs and other interfering substances are listed in the literature (IFU — Young DS).
IFU: performance depends on the analyser used.

slides.title: Quality control
bullets: Assayed control sera are run with each series (IFU: SPINTROL H Normal and Pathologic).
If a control falls outside its range, check the instrument, reagents and technique; do not release patient results.
Each laboratory sets its own quality-control scheme and the corrective actions when controls are out of tolerance.

slides.title: Safety
bullets: R1 (diethanolamine): H315 — skin irritation; H318 — serious eye damage; H373 — may damage organs through prolonged or repeated exposure.
Serum and plasma are potentially infectious: wear gloves and never pipette by mouth.
Follow the precautions in the IFU and the safety data sheet (SDS) when handling the reagents.
Used cuvettes, tubes and tips are disinfected.
